**Visual observations from test image:**
- End (tip) cross-section view of a corn ear
- White, fluffy/cottony mold concentrated in the center (tip area, silk channel zone)
- Kernels appear bleached/grayish with subtle pinkish-reddish tones
- Some kernel wrinkling/damage visible

**Analysis against candidates:**

- **Fusarium**: White to pink/salmon cottony mold on kernels; starburst pattern on individual kernels; scattered or clustered
- **Ear_rots_Gibberella**: Pinkish-white to pink-red mold at the TIP specifically, infecting via silk channel; pink to red kernel streaking
- **Ear_rots_Diplodia**: White mold starting at the BASE (not tip) — doesn't fit

The infection is centered at the tip/silk channel entry point — the classic Gibberella entry route. The kernels show pinkish/reddish discoloration. However, the mold appears more white than distinctly pink/red, leaning toward Fusarium. The reference image for Gibberella showed dark husk material, not the white cottony mold seen here.

The white cottony mold clustered at the tip/center with pinkish kernel coloring is most consistent with **Fusarium** ear rot, which shows white to salmon cottony mold and can concentrate around the tip when insect damage is present there.
